description: Chart pins in stack/*/*/install.sh. Renovate ships no manager that reads a version out of a shell script, and this repo keeps every pin there by design — explicit install scripts are the point, so the fix is to teach Renovate the shape rather than move the pins.

Every chart version in this repo lives in an install.sh, and mirror-check.py skips anything declared kx-only in stack/upstream.json — so without a customManager the kx-only charts (argo-cd, cloudnative-pg, ingress-nginx, kube-prometheus-stack, minio, nats, trust-manager) have no currency instrument at all.
One `helm repo add` per file is what lets the URL and the chart be captured separately without a backreference. Renovate's regex engine is RE2, which has none.

customManagers.description: The same pins for charts pulled straight from an OCI registry, where there is no `helm repo add` line and the chart reference is the image path.

description: Version pins in stack/*/*/install.sh that are not a chart. gateway-api-crds applies a release manifest by URL, so it carries a real pin with no `helm repo add`, no `oci://` and no `--version` flag — the shapes the two chart managers key on. Left unmatched it is a version fetched on every `task up` that nothing watches.

The version assignment and the repository are captured from separate lines because the URL interpolates the variable rather than spelling the version out. Ordered assignment-then-URL to match how the file reads; RE2 has no backreferences, so the two captures cannot be tied together any other way.

kubeconform is fetched by release URL in ci.yml, not by `uses:`, so neither the github-actions manager nor the chart regexes above can see it. Left unwatched it is a version pinned somewhere no instrument looks, drifting until someone happens to read the line.
It is the schema gate's only external binary, and a gate whose validator silently ages is worse than no gate, because the green tick keeps arriving.

customManagers.description: Container images in the manifests kx applies directly. These are not chart pins, so neither the helm managers above nor any Renovate preset sees them — and an image is the one dependency that changes what runs without changing anything a reader would diff.

description: Group the local stack's chart bumps so a slice moves in one PR rather than one per addon, the way the shared preset already groups helm charts elsewhere.

Deliberately sets nothing but groupName. The preset warns that a consumer's packageRules are appended after its own and later rules win — a local rule setting automerge would defeat the security rule that must stay last. This sets no schedule either: the preset already extends schedule:weekly, and a schedule here would also land on CVE-triggered updates, which are meant to fire at any time.

Cilium moves alone, and it does not move ahead of the catalog. eks-gitops ungroups it for reasons that are half local: a CNI minor cannot be reviewed, staged or reverted independently once it is inside a batch, and this is the one chart every pod's networking depends on. The other half of its reasoning — a second pin in landing-zone's cluster-bootstrap, and Cilium's rule that upgrades go consecutive-minor with the newest patch first — does not apply here, because kind installs Cilium straight from this install.sh and there is no second pin to skew against.

The reason that is kx's alone is the mirror. This workspace exists to validate against the shape eks-gitops actually ships, so bumping a chart the catalog deliberately holds does not merely risk a broken kind cluster — it breaks what kx is for. Without this rule cilium rides the kx-stack-charts group, and Without this rule cilium rides the kx-stack-charts group and can move ahead of the catalog inside a batch. mirror-check catches the divergence afterwards, but by then the reason is gone and the next reader re-derives it from scratch — which is what the hold recorded in eks-gitops#207 exists to prevent.

dependencyDashboardApproval rather than enabled:false. The update stays on the Dependency Dashboard with a checkbox, visible and releasable the moment the catalog moves. Disabling the package makes the update silently stop existing, which is a worse failure than holding it in the open.

This rule is placed after the grouping rule on purpose: a consumer's packageRules are appended after the preset's and later rules win, which is what lets groupName: null pull cilium back out of a group set above.
